quotes.text: CSR becomes real only when it becomes measurable. The moment you can measure something, you can budget it. The moment you can budget it, you can enforce it.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: States the episode's core thesis that measurement turns values into control.

quotes.text: If sustainability lives in a report, it's optional. If sustainability lives in a budget line, it's real. The moment carbon has an internal price, engineers feel it without being asked to care.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Explains why internal carbon pricing changes engineering behavior.

quotes.text: Treat carbon as a non-functional requirement, alongside latency, security, and resiliency. Not a report, a requirement.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters

quotes.text: Every duplicated flow, every zombie app, every temporary automation that runs forever is compute. It schedules jobs. It triggers API calls. It writes data.

quotes.text: If carbon were priced like cost, would you still deploy it this way? That question is the entire control plane in one line.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters

takeaways: Corporate social responsibility only becomes real when it is measurable, budgeted and enforced through procurement, architecture and finance decisions.

Microsoft's internal carbon fee, carbon accounting across scopes 1 to 3, removal procurement and Cloud for Sustainability form a carbon control plane, but AI-driven growth makes the audit a moving target.
Organizations can copy the mechanics, not the slogans: treat carbon as a non-functional requirement, review one workload with one owner, and set region and runtime defaults that make waste expensive.
hook: Microsoft promised to be carbon negative, yet its emissions rose as AI and data centers scaled, which makes auditing its footprint a real governance problem. This episode is for sustainability leads, cloud architects and Microsoft 365 admins who want to understand the internal carbon fee, scope 3 accounting, carbon removals and Cloud for Sustainability, and how to apply a carbon-per-workload review in their own tenant.
